support_summary: D6: single-author letter in which the same author prompted ChatGPT and judged the references, with no duplicate or blinded verification and no agreement figure (Author contribution; Par40); D1/D2/D3/D4/D7: one author-chosen yohimbine/CYP2D6 topic pursued through conversational follow-up prompts printed verbatim, model given as free ChatGPT Version 1.2024.170 (GPT-4o) on a Mac with no generation date and no generation settings reported (Par1), verification shown only by the narrative that all 5 titles do not exist while the authors and journals are real and the PubMed IDs belong to different authors, topics and journals, with no second-source or partial-match rule stated (Par40), although all 5 references are listed in full.

D4: no bibliographic verification source is named for the sources or references the chatbots provided - correctness was judged by the two authors as experts and only the number of responses providing sources is counted (Materials and Methods; Table 2); D1/D2/D3/D5/D6/D7: 10 author-prepared audiology questions printed in full (Table 1) presented on 28.08.2023 to standard public ChatGPT 3.5, Bing Chat (GPT-4) and Bard (PaLM 2) with no exact Bing or Bard version strings and no generation settings, the two authors both presented the questions and rated the responses, going over them twice and agreeing scores with no blinding and no agreement figure, and no partial-match rule or separate partial counts for references, although all 3 models and all 10 questions are reported including Bard failing to answer one question (Table 2; Discussion).
